call.transcript: There's a house on fire at 4th and Main! The whole second floor is engulfed, flames are shooting out the windows. I don't know if anyone is still inside!
Oh god there's a massive fire on Main Avenue near 4th Street. Huge flames coming out of a house, black smoke everywhere. I'm right outside, I already saw someone calling 911 but I'm calling too.

notes: Different passerby reporting the same 4th & Main house fire from outside

call.transcript: Oh my god okay I'm in my apartment and the fire alarm just went off and I looked out my door and the hallway is FULL of smoke, I can't see more than five feet in front of me. I'm on the sixth floor of Oak Street Apartments. I don't know where the fire is but the smoke is really thick and black and it smells like burning plastic. My neighbor tried to use the elevator and it opened and there was smoke pouring out of it. I have asthma and I'm already having trouble breathing just in my doorway. My husband is trying to reach the stairwell to see if it's clear. There are two small children in the apartment across the hall from me and I knocked but nobody answered. Please send help NOW, we need firefighters with ladders, and we need ambulances because people up here are going to need oxygen. I don't know how many people are in this building but it's a big complex, completely full.

notes: Long rambling call — caller is trapped on 6th floor with asthma, children unaccounted for

call.transcript: Fire at Union Station! The west wing storage area is fully on fire. I'm a station employee and we've evacuated the main concourse but there are still workers in the basement. Flames are visible through the windows on the ground floor.

notes: Caller is an employee with specific situational knowledge — workers still unaccounted for in basement

call.transcript: Car on fire on Highway 9, somewhere near mile marker 12. I don't know if anyone is inside — the driver's door is open which maybe means they got out? But I honestly can't tell. The engine compartment is fully on fire and it's spreading to the passenger area.

notes: Ambiguous severity — occupant status unclear, open door suggests escape but not confirmed

call.transcript: Uh, there's a dumpster on fire behind Lincoln Elementary School. It's like, pretty big already, and the dumpster is maybe six feet from the wooden fence. The wind is picking up. I don't see any kids around — school's out — but if it jumps that fence it could hit the building.

notes: Ambiguous severity — contained dumpster fire but proximity to wooden fence and building could escalate

call.transcript: Fire in Riverside Park! The dry grass caught and it's spreading really fast toward the tree line. I'd estimate it's already fifty feet wide and growing. The wind is not helping. There are some people running away from it near the south trail.

PLEASE HURRY there's a fire at my neighbor's house! I'm at... oh god... it's 5th and Maple? No wait, it's 5th and Broadway, the house with the green shutters! The whole front porch is on fire and I can hear children screaming inside. I can't get to the door, the fire is blocking it. PLEASE.

notes: Conflicting address — caller gives two intersections before correcting; children audibly inside

call.transcript: Um, I'm standing outside City Hall Plaza and there's a lot of smoke coming out of a second-floor window. I don't see any flames at all, it could be nothing? Like maybe an overheated piece of equipment? But it smells weird, kind of chemical. There's no alarm going off as far as I can tell.

notes: Ambiguous severity — smoke present but caller doubts themselves; no visible flames, no alarm

call.transcript: Garage fire at the corner of Maple and 3rd. The garage is fully involved but I'm pretty sure no one is inside, the family ran out. The flames are licking the side wall of the main house now though. You need to move fast.
MY HUSBAND ISN'T BREATHING. RIVERSIDE HOSPITAL PARKING LOT. PLEASE HURRY.

notes: Extremely terse — clear critical severity despite minimal words; location and chief complaint unambiguous

call.transcript: There's a man collapsed in the parking lot outside Riverside Hospital. I was walking to my car and I found him. He's not breathing and another woman who stopped says she's a nurse and she's doing CPR. Please send an ambulance to the Riverside Hospital parking lot right away.

notes: Bystander reporting same incident — observational, calmer tone; CPR already in progress confirms same event

call.transcript: My baby is choking! She can't breathe, she's turning blue! We're at the Westside Mall food court, I don't know exactly where but we're right by the Chinese place. She's three years old, she was eating a grape. Please come NOW.

I think my roommate overdosed. He's on the floor in the hallway and he's completely unresponsive, barely breathing. I can't wake him up at all. We're at Oak Street Apartments, apartment 4B. I don't know what he took but there are pills scattered around him. Please hurry.

My friend took something at the Eastside Community Center, I don't know what it was. She's technically awake but she's really out of it — slurring her words, her eyes keep rolling back. She keeps saying she's fine but she's not fine. She might be getting worse.

notes: Ambiguous severity — patient conscious and denying emergency, but showing signs of deterioration

call.transcript: My mother fell down the stairs and I cannot wake her up! She is 82 years old and not responding to anything. We were just leaving the senior center at City Hall Plaza. There is blood on the back of her head. She fell from the top of the staircase.

Guy fell off a ladder at the construction site near Memorial Bridge. He's conscious, he's talking to us, and his leg is obviously broken — the bone might be through the skin, hard to look at. His arm might be broken too. He's in a lot of pain but he's alert and stable.

notes: Non-critical MEDICAL — patient conscious, alert, and stable despite serious orthopedic injuries

call.transcript: Something is very wrong with my father. He woke up and one side of his face is completely drooping. He tried to raise his arm and couldn't lift it. He's trying to talk but it's all garbled, I can't understand him. I think he's having a stroke. We're at 5th and Broadway.

My son got stung by a bee near Riverside Park, right at the park entrance. He's allergic and he used his EpiPen but his throat is still swelling. He's having trouble breathing and his lips look puffy. The Epi bought some time but he needs a hospital right now.

There's a homeless man passed out by the fountain at Central Park Entrance. I shook his shoulder and he did not respond at all. I can't tell if he's breathing. His lips are a little blue. He might have been out here for a while, I don't know.

My coworker is acting really strange at Jefferson High gymnasium, we're using it for a community event. She's confused, she's shaking, sweating a lot. She mentioned diabetes before she started getting bad. She's sitting up and can say a few words but she seems really out of it. I don't know if this is an emergency or if she just needs juice or something.

notes: Ambiguous severity — possible hypoglycemia, patient responsive; caller uncertain if intervention needed

call.transcript: Oh my god okay so my wife is 38 weeks pregnant and her water broke about twenty minutes ago and her contractions are already two minutes apart, and we were trying to get to the hospital but our car wouldn't start so we walked to the Eastside Community Center because it was close, and now she's saying the baby is coming RIGHT NOW, she's screaming and she says she can feel the head, and I've never done this before, I have absolutely no idea what to do, I'm panicking, she's on the floor in the lobby, the center address is on Eastside Avenue I think, there's a sign out front. Can you please please send someone who knows what they're doing, I'm completely alone here and she says it's happening now. I need you to tell me what to do until they get here.

notes: Long rambling call — imminent delivery, panicked first-time father, location confirmed

call.transcript: Car accident at 4th and Main, two cars collided, one of them ran a red light. There are people hurt — I can see at least two people injured, one woman is bleeding from her head and another passenger is holding his arm. I'm going to see if I can help.

Bad crash at Main and 4th Street — looks like two cars hit each other hard, one ran a light I think. I can see at least one person who looks injured, slumped over in the driver's seat. Other car's airbags went off.

notes: Different witness, different vantage point — slightly fewer injuries visible from their angle

call.transcript: A car just hit a pedestrian at Memorial Bridge! The person flew about fifteen feet and they are NOT moving. The car stopped. There is blood on the road. The pedestrian is completely still and unresponsive. Please hurry, I don't think this person is breathing!

Hi, um, there's been a minor car accident near Union Station. Two cars bumped into each other in the side street. Both drivers are out and walking around and nobody seems to be hurt. Just a lot of bumper damage. Can you send someone for the police report?

Motorcyclist down on Highway 9 near mile marker 12. He skidded out, he's on the ground. His helmet is cracked. He's conscious and he's yelling but his leg looks very bad, probably a compound fracture. He cannot get up. Bike is still running in the road.

A child on a bicycle just got hit by a car at 5th and Broadway! The kid is maybe eight years old, he's crying and has road rash all up his arms. The driver pulled over. The kid wasn't wearing a helmet and his head might have hit the pavement. He seems conscious but confused.

Oh god there has been a massive pile-up on Highway 9 near mile marker 12, it just happened, like two minutes ago. I counted four or maybe five cars plus a jackknifed semi. There's glass everywhere, steam from engines, and I can see people trapped in at least two of the vehicles. One car is completely on its side. I can hear a child crying from inside one of the cars. There's a woman hanging halfway out of a window, not moving. I'm a registered nurse and I'm going to try to help but I need backup immediately. And listen — there is fuel leaking from the semi, I can smell it, this could turn into a fire. You need to send fire trucks too, not just ambulances. This is a mass casualty situation. Please send everything you have.

notes: Long rambling call from medical professional — mass casualty, fuel leak fire risk, child trapped

call.transcript: A car just hit someone and drove off! Near Riverside Park, right on the riverside road. The victim is a woman, she's on the ground, she's conscious but her leg is clearly broken and she's screaming in pain. The car was a red sedan, it just kept going toward downtown.

Big truck rolled over on the exit ramp near Memorial Bridge. The driver is okay — he climbed out himself — but he's sitting on the ground looking really dazed and confused. Maybe a concussion? The truck is blocking both lanes of the ramp. No other vehicles involved.

A car just drove through a storefront window! I think it's on Old Town Square... actually it might be on 5th Avenue, they're right next to each other. There is a person pinned between the car and the counter inside, they are screaming. Several people are inside the store. You need fire and ambulance.

notes: Conflicting location — caller gives Old Town Square then second-guesses to 5th Avenue

call.transcript: ROBBERY UNION STATION RIGHT NOW. GUY HAS A GUN. HURRY.

notes: Extremely terse — caller likely hiding or whispering; location and threat type clear

call.transcript: Someone is beating a man outside the Downtown Parking Garage on 5th! The attacker has a metal pipe and the victim is on the ground and he is not getting up. The attacker is still hitting him. There is blood on the concrete. Please come right now, this man is going to die!

Someone is breaking into my house right now! I can hear them smashing the back window. I'm locked in my bedroom with my two children. We're at the corner of 7th and Elm, the gas station corner house, gray house. I'm terrified, please hurry!

Hi, I want to report something suspicious near Riverside Park. There's a man who's been sitting in a dark car for about two hours just watching the playground. He drives away and comes back. I might be completely overreacting, I don't know. He hasn't done anything that I've seen. Just... it doesn't feel right.

notes: Ambiguous severity — no confirmed threat or criminal act; caller themselves unsure

call.transcript: My neighbor is in trouble. I can hear her screaming and something breaking — furniture maybe. It went quiet for a minute and I was going to call back but then it started again. She's screaming for help. They're at... I think 6th Street Apartments? No wait, it's Oak Street Apartments, Building B, second floor. Please send someone, I've called before about these two but tonight it sounds really bad.

notes: Conflicting address — caller gives wrong building first; prior incident history mentioned

call.transcript: Shots fired at Westside Mall! I heard at least three or four gunshots near the food court, maybe five minutes ago. People are running and screaming everywhere. I locked myself in a back office of a store. I don't know if anyone has been shot, I can't see. The mall is full of people.

Two men just carjacked me at the gas station on 7th and Elm. One of them had a knife. They pulled me right out of the driver's seat. I'm okay, I wasn't hurt, just really shaken. My kids were NOT in the car, thank god. The car went north on Elm toward the highway.

Man has been stabbed at City Hall Plaza! He's on the ground, holding his stomach, there's a lot of blood. The person who did it ran toward Old Town. The victim is conscious, he's talking, but he's losing blood fast. Hurry please.

There's a strong gas smell coming from the basement of Oak Street Apartments. I mean really strong — the whole hallway reeks, not just a whiff. We've evacuated our floor but I have no idea about the other floors. Someone might still be in the building. Please bring hazmat, this is not a small leak.

A power line came down on Maple Avenue at 3rd Street, probably from the wind. It's on the pavement and it's sparking. The road is blocked — cars stopped on both sides. Nobody is hurt as far as I can tell but people are getting out of their cars to look at it.

Chemical spill at the Industrial District, near the loading docks. A large drum fell off a forklift and it's leaking something yellowish. Workers are coughing and rubbing their eyes. We've moved everyone upwind but there's a visible yellow vapor cloud forming near the dock. We don't know what the chemical is.

The underpass at Memorial Bridge is flooding fast. The water is already up to the hood level of the cars down there. A few drivers got out of their cars and are standing on the curb but their cars are basically underwater now. The water is still rising and the road is completely impassable.

A large tree fell across the road at the Riverside Park entrance. It's blocking the whole road completely. There are some power lines tangled in the branches but I don't see sparking. Nobody is hurt, nobody is around. The road is just totally blocked.

I'm calling about a fire at Oak Street Apartments — I'm a neighbor across the street. I can see smoke pouring out of multiple windows on what looks like the fifth or sixth floor. People are on the fire escape. I can hear alarms going off. This looks really serious.

notes: Neighbor across the street reporting the same fire — exterior view confirms multiple floors affected

call.transcript: I'm the driver — I hit a pedestrian at Memorial Bridge. I didn't see him, he stepped out from between parked cars. I stopped immediately. He's on the ground and he's not moving. I'm right here with him. Oh god please hurry, I don't know what to do, there's a lot of blood.

notes: Driver calling in — confirms same incident from at-fault party's perspective

call.transcript: I work at Westside Mall and I'm locked in the back of a clothing store. I heard gunshots near the food court — at least three of them. I can hear people screaming and running in the hallway outside my door. I'm hiding behind a rack of clothes. Is someone already coming? Please tell me someone is coming.

notes: Employee hidden in different part of mall — confirms shots heard, active panic in building

call.transcript: This is the building manager at Oak Street Apartments. A tenant just reported a strong gas odor from the basement level. I went down to check and I can confirm it — very strong smell of natural gas in the utility corridor. I am evacuating the building now. We need gas company and fire department immediately.

notes: Building manager confirms same gas leak — professional caller, initiating evacuation

call.transcript: There's a man being attacked outside the parking garage on 5th Avenue. The attacker ran when I shouted but the victim is still on the ground. He's conscious but he's bleeding from his head and he can't get up. I think the attacker used something, not his fists. Please send police and an ambulance.

notes: Bystander who shouted at attacker — attacker fled; caller arrived mid-event
